title: Extensively degenerate superradiant phase in a giant-atom quantum Rabi ring
abstract: We show that an $N$-site quantum Rabi ring with matched giant-atom couplings has $2^N$ degenerate superradiant configurations as the atomic-to-cavity frequency ratio $η=Δ/ω$ tends to infinity. Each atom couples to two cavities two sites apart, and the photon hopping carries a phase $π/2$. Tuning the ratio of contact strengths to the photon hopping reduces the mean-field energy to a sum of single-site Rabi energies, with a common critical coupling for all momentum-pair sectors. The degeneracy survives quadratic quantum fluctuations despite a dispersive excitation spectrum. At finite $η$, second-order processes involving the local cubic anharmonicity generate a same-sublattice Ising coupling of order $ω/η$, selecting ferro- and antiferro-superradiant configurations. This quantum order-by-disorder effect has no classical counterpart. Four-site calculations retaining all spin states quantitatively support the predicted energy coefficients. The separation between the induced coupling and the excitation gap allows a broad temperature interval with macroscopic photon occupation and short-range correlations between displacement signs.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the superradiant phase in a quantum Rabi ring, showing that the system possesses extensive degeneracy in the mean-field limit. Crucially, it demonstrates that quantum fluctuations introduce a non-classical Ising coupling that selects between ferro- and antiferro-superradiant states. The methodology combines mean-field theory with advanced quantum perturbation techniques.
main_problem: The study investigates the superradiant phase transition and the extensive degeneracy of superradiant configurations in an N-site quantum Rabi ring.
main_result: The system exhibits extensive degeneracy in the mean-field limit ($\eta 	o \infty$), which is stabilized by quantum fluctuations, and finite-frequency corrections select specific ferro- or antiferro-superradiant states via a quantum order-by-disorder effect.
method: The analysis employs mean-field theory, followed by a Schrieffer–Wolff transformation and second-order perturbation theory to derive an effective Ising Hamiltonian describing quantum corrections.
model_or_system: The model is an N-site quantum Rabi ring with two-level atoms, where each atom couples to two cavities two sites apart. The system is governed by a Hamiltonian involving cavity fields and atomic spins.
key_observables: Superradiant excitation gap ($\varepsilon_{\min}$), effective Ising coupling constants ($J_r$), and the degeneracy of superradiant configurations.
important_parameters: The atomic-to-cavity frequency ratio $\eta = \Delta/\omega$, and the coupling ratio $ eta$ that determines the phase (FSR, AFSR, CSR).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mean-field approximation and subsequent quantum corrections derived via perturbation theory, assuming the photon band remains dispersive.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model setup, momentum-dependent critical coupling, phase diagrams, and show the evolution of correlation lengths and sign structure factors distinguishing different superradiant phases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the mean-field degeneracy in the infinite limit, to deriving the effective low-energy Hamiltonian using quantum corrections, and finally analyzing the resulting quantum order-by-disorder selection mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how quantum fluctuations can stabilize and select specific ordered phases (FSR/AFSR) in cavity QED systems, demonstrating a quantum order-by-disorder effect absent classically.
